accepted.s:
The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, provides for the establishment of the National Tribunals Commission. Which one of the following is correct regarding its composition and tenure?
1. Its headquarters will be at New Delhi.
2. It will consist of five members.
3. The tenure will be five years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The National Tribunals Commission under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, has its headquarters at New Delhi, consists of five members and provides a five-year or 70-year age limit for tenure.
accepted.tq: Use the statement-combination method and verify each institutional detail separately.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, was introduced primarily to replace which of the following?
accepted.x: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, replaces the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.
accepted.tq: Identify the replacing legislation rather than the institutional body created by it.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026:
1. It changes the name of Kerala to Keralam.
2. The change was approved by the Lok Sabha on 11 August 2026 and by the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.
3. The name of the High Court is also changed by the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Act changes Kerala to Keralam, with Lok Sabha approval on 11 August and Rajya Sabha approval on 12 August 2026. The High Court name remains unchanged.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the exception relating to the High Court.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, operates through an alteration in which constitutional provision and Schedule?
accepted.x: The change from Kerala to Keralam is made under Article 3 and involves the First Schedule of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Apply the article-and-Schedule pairing technique used for constitutional amendments.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment, 2026, provides for which of the following penalties for specified offences?
o: Two to five years' imprisonment and a fine up to ₹10 lakh
Life imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh
Five to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine up to ₹1 crore
Five to ten years' imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh
accepted.x: The amendment provides for imprisonment of five to ten years and a fine of up to ₹50 lakh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact punishment range and monetary ceiling.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment, 2026, investigation of an unfair-means case is to be completed within:
accepted.x: The amendment requires the probe to be completed within 60 days and provides for special fast-track courts.
accepted.tq: Use the precise statutory time-limit as the distinguishing fact.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025?
o: It replaces MGNREGA from 1 July 2026 and provides 125 days of employment with a base wage of ₹300 per day.
It replaces MGNREGA from 1 January 2026 and provides 100 days of employment with a base wage of ₹250 per day.
It supplements MGNREGA from 1 July 2026 and provides 150 days of employment with a base wage of ₹300 per day.
It replaces the National Food Security Act from 1 July 2026 and provides 125 days of employment.
accepted.x: The VB-G RAM G Act replaces MGNREGA from 1 July 2026, provides 125 days of employment and fixes a base wage of ₹300 per day.
accepted.tq: Separate the effective date, employment guarantee and wage figure before selecting the complete option.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, is associated with which of the following provisions?
o: Regulation of only educational online games
A ban on real-money games and establishment of an Online Gaming Authority of India under the 2026 Rules
Transfer of online gaming regulation exclusively to State Governments
A ban on all forms of online games, including recreational games
accepted.x: The Act bans real-money games, while the 2026 Rules establish the Online Gaming Authority of India from 1 May 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a targeted prohibition from an exaggerated ban on every online game.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025, replaced which of the following laws?
o: Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
Atomic Energy Act, 1948 and Nuclear Safety Act, 2010
Electricity Act, 2003 and Atomic Energy Act, 1962
Environment Protection Act, 1986 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
accepted.x: The SHANTI Act, 2025, replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of Acts replaced by the new legislation.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the SHANTI Act, 2025?
o: A limited role for private entities
Unlimited supplier liability for nuclear damage
A liability cap of 300 million SDR
accepted.x: The SHANTI Act provides for no supplier liability, a limited private role and a cap of 300 million SDR; it does not impose unlimited supplier liability.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the central liability provision.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026, increased the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to:
accepted.x: The amendment increases the Supreme Court strength from 34 to 38, comprising 37 judges apart from the Chief Justice of India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total strength from the number of judges excluding the CJI.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026, amended which legislation?
o: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956
accepted.x: The 2026 amendment amended the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, in connection with Article 124.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with the parent statute rather than the constitutional article alone.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment), 2026, makes insulting or disrupting which of the following punishable?
accepted.x: The amendment to the 1971 Act makes insulting or disrupting Vande Mataram punishable.
accepted.tq: Use the exact protected national symbol instead of substituting a more familiar one.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The MMDR Amendment, 2026, is primarily concerned with which subject and ministry?
o: Critical minerals fiscal regime — Ministry of Mines
Coal mine rehabilitation — Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Rare earth research — Ministry of Science and Technology
accepted.x: The MMDR Amendment, 2026, establishes a fiscal regime for critical minerals and is associated with the Ministry of Mines.
accepted.tq: Match the legislative subject with the responsible ministry.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following amendments removes self-determination of gender?
accepted.x: The Transgender Persons (Amendment), 2026, removes self-determination of gender; the amendment was made in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Apply the provision to the legislation most directly connected with the subject.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, provides that which of the following shall be the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Act declares Amaravati to be the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh, retrospectively from 2 June 2024.
accepted.tq: Identify the location and separately note the retrospective effective date.
accepted.sec: Bills passed by Parliament - name, ministry, objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the adjudicating authority for insolvency resolution is the:
o: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
accepted.x: The National Company Law Tribunal is the adjudicating authority under the IBC. Appeals lie to the NCLAT, and resolution is intended to occur within 180 to 330 days.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original adjudicating body from the appellate body.
accepted.sec: Acts in news - provisions, amending Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relationship between the NCLT and NCLAT under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
o: NCLAT is the adjudicating authority and NCLT is the appellate forum.
NCLAT functions as the appellate forum against orders of NCLT.
Both bodies function only as advisory bodies.
accepted.x: The NCLT acts as the adjudicating authority, while appeals against its orders lie before the NCLAT.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the adjudicating and appellate authorities.
accepted.sec: Acts in news - provisions, amending Acts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fast-track courts in India:
1. There are 884 fast-track courts in 21 States and Union Territories.
2. These courts have 17.54 lakh pending cases.
3. They function only in matters relating to taxation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: There are 884 fast-track courts in 21 States and Union Territories with 17.54 lakh pending cases. Their jurisdiction is not limited only to taxation matters.
accepted.tq: Reject the overbroad subject restriction and retain the reported numerical facts.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is implemented through the collaboration of which two institutions?
o: Supreme Court e-Committee and National Informatics Centre
Law Commission and Election Commission of India
NITI Aayog and National Human Rights Commission
Department of Justice and Finance Commission
accepted.x: The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is a joint initiative of the Supreme Court e-Committee and the National Informatics Centre.
accepted.tq: Match the digital justice project with its institutional partners.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many virtual courts for petty offences are associated with the e-Courts Mission Mode Project?
accepted.x: The e-Courts Mission Mode Project includes 30 virtual courts dealing with petty offences.
accepted.tq: Test the exact count instead of the broader concept of virtual courts.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court functions fully in virtual mode on which of the following days?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court is fully virtual on Mondays and Fridays.
accepted.tq: Use the weekday pair as the precise distinguishing detail.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. One Case One Data — Supreme Court initiative
2. Su Sahayak — launched by the Supreme Court
3. Draft rules on AI in judiciary — June 2026
4. Four new Division Benches — July 2026
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Supreme Court launched One Case One Data and Su Sahayak in May 2026, issued draft AI rules in June 2026 and added four Division Benches in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Confirm each date-and-initiative pair before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the India Justice Report 2025, which one of the following correctly represents the judicial infrastructure indicators?
o: About 15 judges per million people, fewer than 2,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases
About 25 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 3.5 crore pending cases
About 15 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases
About 10 judges per million people, more than 7,600 vacancies and over 4.5 crore pending cases
accepted.x: The India Justice Report 2025 records approximately 15 judges per million people, more than 5,600 vacancies and over 5.5 crore pending cases.
accepted.tq: Compare all three numerical indicators as a single data set.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Collegium system is correct?
o: It is expressly provided in the Constitution and was established in 1950.
It was created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment and replaced by the NJAC in 2015.
It was established through an Act of Parliament in 1998.
It is not expressly mentioned in the Constitution and emerged through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 judgment.
accepted.x: The Collegium system is not expressly provided in the Constitution; it evolved through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 decision. The NJAC created by the 99th Amendment was struck down in 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate constitutional text from judicially evolved practice.
accepted.sec: Judicial infrastructure - virtual courts, e-courts, fast-track courts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The renaming of Jonnagiri Gold Mine in Andhra Pradesh as Swarnagiri Gold Mine was undertaken in:
accepted.x: Jonnagiri Gold Mine was renamed Swarnagiri Gold Mine in July 2026 by the CDCA.
accepted.tq: Match the renaming event with its exact month and year.
accepted.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Nauru was renamed in August 2026 as:
accepted.x: Nauru was renamed the Republic of Naoero in August 2026.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official form of the renamed country.
accepted.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Scheme for Promotion of International Cultural Relations was renamed as:
accepted.x: The Scheme for Promotion of International Cultural Relations was renamed the Global Engagement Scheme and is associated with the Ministry of Culture.
accepted.tq: Match the old scheme title with its new official name and ministry context.
accepted.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many districts does Andhra Pradesh have since December 2025?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has 28 districts since December 2025; it had 26 districts from April 2022.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the latest figure from the earlier administrative count.
accepted.sec: Renaming of cities, districts and places  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, was promulgated under which Article of the Constitution?
accepted.x: The Ordinance was promulgated by the President under Article 123 in May 2026. Article 124 relates to the Supreme Court itself and its judges.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ordinance-making Article from the substantive constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026, was replaced by a Bill passed by the Lok Sabha on:
accepted.x: The replacement Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 3 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the exact legislative date to connect the Ordinance with its replacement Bill.
accepted.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

accepted.s: Which Bill replaced the Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026?
accepted.x: The Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, was replaced by the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
accepted.tq: Identify the replacement Bill by matching its title with the Ordinance subject.
accepted.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance — June 2026
2. Sri City University Ordinance — Article 213
3. Supreme Court Number of Judges Ordinance — Article 213
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The AP Human Organ Transplantation Ordinance was promulgated in June 2026, and the Sri City University Ordinance was issued under Article 213. The Supreme Court Ordinance was promulgated under Article 123, not Article 213.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional division between Union and State ordinance powers to detect the swapped Article.
accepted.sec: Ordinances promulgated - subject, Article, replacement Bill
